summary: Ambiguous burst accounting leading to short-lived streaming sessions hitting 429s in eu-west
description:
Issue summary: Customer using a dedicated pool for eu-west is observing a surge of 429s that only affect short-lived streaming (WebSocket) sessions. These 429s started after an ingestion ramp last Thursday and are intermittent across API keys. Impact: Production streaming features (real-time search highlights) are failing for ~12% of requests and causing degraded UX during ingestion windows. Environment: Dedicated pool (eu-west), pool autoscaling enabled, fallback to hosted disabled for this customer. No recent customer-side SDK changes reported.

Observed behaviour is distinct from bulk-batch 429s: failures occur within seconds of connection open and often occur in bursts correlated with a spike in the number of connect/disconnect events rather than total token throughput.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's SDK to open a large number (1000+) of short lived WebSocket streaming sessions targeting eu-west dedicated pool
2) Each session sends an initial prompt and closes within 1-3s
3) Observe 429 responses returned at connect time or within the first response frame for ~10-15% of sessions during peak churn
4) Repeat with long-lived sessions (>=30s) - failure rate drops to <1%
5) Repeat in staging (smaller pool) - failure rate similar when churn is reproduced.

investigation_notes: 2026-02-28 Ava: Confirmed spike correlates with customer ingestion job between 15:50-16:10 UTC; token consumption as reported in console did not show proportional increase to explain 429s
2026-03-01 Diego: Reproduced locally by spawning 2k short WS connects to eu-west dedicated endpoint; observed high 429 rate when connect/disconnect churn > 500/s

2026-03-01 Priya (SRE): Edge-proxy logs show 'release missing reservation' warnings when connections close before the rate-limiter acks reservation - suggests race between connection lifecycle and token reservation bookkeeping

2026-03-01 Hypothesis: Short-lived sessions are counting against a short-window burst bucket tied to route aliasing. Frequent opens before prior reservations are fully garbage-collected cause transient double-accounting or non-decremented entries leading to apparent exhaustion. This is different from per-token charging, it's about concurrency/reservation accounting for streaming sessions.

2026-03-02 Diego: Checked dedicated-pool config - short_burst_window configured to 1s and burst_capacity small (50). Customer's ingestion produced >600 concurrent connects within that 1s window which would exceed burst_capacity even though average throughput tokens/sec is normal.
2026-03-02 Mitigation test: Increase short_burst_window to 2s and burst_capacity to 800 in a control cluster - observed connect 429 rate drop from 12% to 0.8% during synthetic churn.
comments: 2026-02-28 17:05 - Support (Ava Bennett): Acknowledged ticket and requested connection timings and sample API-keys from customer. Asked for a short window of elevated logs and the ingestion schedule.
2026-03-01 09:20 - Customer (J. Müller, GlobeSearch): Sent ingestion details and confirmed they did not change SDK; we provided sample traffic generator and test credentials.
2026-03-01 13:44 - SRE (Priya Nair): Noted 'release missing reservation' entries in edge logs; flagged for Diego to reproduce against dedicated pool.

2026-03-01 18:30 - Infra (Diego Ramirez): Reproduced locally; recommended temporary workaround (client-level): recommend increasing connection keepalive to >10s or implement multiplexing so fewer short-lived sessions are opened.
2026-03-02 08:12 - Support (Ava Bennett): Communicated workaround and asked customer to coordinate a 30-minute ingestion retest window tomorrow morning UTC.
2026-03-02 14:05 - Customer (J. Müller): Performed retest with increased keepalive; reported failure rate fell to ~1.2% and UX acceptable. Requested longer-term fix and configuration guidance.

2026-03-02 16:40 - Diego Ramirez: Filed an infra action to evaluate rate-limiter bookkeeping for connection lifecycle edge-cases and drafted a patch to change reservation GC to be idempotent on close. Linked PR in related_github_prs.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer implemented longer-lived streaming sessions and reduced connection churn; temporary burst_capacity increase tested in control cluster. Root cause: rate-limiter short-window burst capacity and reservation GC race on connection close caused transient token-accounting exhaustion for high-churn short-lived streaming sessions. Next steps: infra patch to make reservation release idempotent and to add a 'streaming' route tag that uses separate burst buckets for ephemeral WS sessions. Planning rollout via canary to dedicated pools. Customer will keep longer keepalive until fix is deployed.
follow_up_tasks: INF-3210: Implement idempotent reservation release and add telemetry for missing_release events
INF-3211: Add per-route streaming burst bucket option + documentation update
DOC-441: Guidance doc for customers on best practices for streaming vs multiplexing to avoid burst throttles
